title: Engagement page: single landing for classifier, factory, and newsroom offers
description: One page that says what an engagement looks like (pilot scope, what a first month produces, how to start) with one call to action. The Plexus, Kanbus, and Papyrus articles all end here. Replaces the generic contact link to the bio page as the article CTA. Coordinate with 1b53c5 (homepage one job, one CTA) and c6739d (foundational messaging) so the hire path is consistent.

comments.author: unknown
comments.text:
Built the engagement page and article CTA funnel.

Created:
- src/pages/engage.js + src/pages/engage.module.css: /engage landing page. Sections: what an engagement is, three offer blocks (Classifier lab on Plexus / Factory-run software project / Newsroom for a publication), 'What a first month produces', single CTA button using centralised contactUrl.
- src/components/contact-url.js: centralises contactUrl (same Google Form URL). Imported by engage.js and ai-solutions.js (index.js untouched per instructions).
- src/components/engage-cta.jsx + engage-cta.module.css: boxed end-of-article CTA linking to /engage.

Changed:
- src/pages/ai-solutions.js: now imports contactUrl from the new shared module instead of defining it locally.
- src/templates/blog-post.jsx: added tags to the GraphQL frontmatter query, imports EngageCTA, and renders it after the article body only when frontmatter.tags includes 'client-acquisition'. Confirmed via gatsby-node.js that blog-post.jsx is the only template used for both posts and articles (templates/article.jsx is unused/dead), so this is the single wiring point.
- src/site-content/distilling-jev-into-a-classifier.mdx: added 'client-acquisition' tag alongside the existing tags (kept the 'research' tag another agent added concurrently).

Did not touch: navigation/header/footer, src/pages/index.js, src/pages/research.js, and did not implement anything from parked 959bf4/1b53c5.

Verification: npx prettier --write/--check on all new/changed JS/JSX files - clean. Did not run npm run build or npm run dev per instructions (parent session builds).

Left in_progress for parent session review before build/merge.
